($) STATE GOVERNMENT Editorial: "Robert Roberson hearing raises profound questions about guilt ," via Dallas Morning News -- "Had Robert Roberson III been executed by the state of Texas last Thursday night as scheduled, it would have been a shameful failure of our criminal justice system. Out of appeals, Roberson would have been put to death even as his conviction on outdated "shaken baby syndrome" science in the death of his 2-year-old daughter was shrouded in tremendous doubt. Instead, a bipartisan group of Texas lawmakers, some of whom actually support the death penalty, boldly prevented that from happening. Their to issue a subpoena requiring Roberson to testify before the House Committee on Criminal Jurisprudence effectively stayed the execution, at least for now. The unprecedented move, led by Rep. Joe Moody , D-El Paso, and Rep. Jeff Leach , R-Plano, to effectively go around the state's judicial branch does raise valid questions about a potential violation of the state's constitutionally enshrined separation of powers among the legislative, judicial and executive branches. Those concerns may well be headed for a full airing in court, as the Texas Supreme Court noted . But if ever there was a case to test the limits of those separations, it's this one. The fact is, it should have never come to all of this. The House committee hearing has brought into full public view, on live-streamed video, a distressing set of facts surrounding Roberson's case and the way the criminal justice system has dug into his conviction. The committee is studying whether the state's "junk science" law, that provides a pathway for new trials for those convicted on the basis of discredited science, has worked as intended in Roberson's case. In 2003, an Anderson County jury convicted Roberson in the death of his daughter largely on a doctor's diagnosis that she had suffered from "shaken baby syndrome." Back then, doctors believed the syndrome was the only explanation for three different types of internal head injuries in small children, absent a serious accident. But today, doctors realize that these same symptoms can be caused by other things, as well. Roberson's attorneys contend that the jury never heard evidence of some of those causes, and that the district attorney rushed to convict. Even Roberson's defense attorney said at trial that this was a textbook "shaken baby" case, though his client maintained his innocence and rejected plea bargain deals. Roberson's attorneys today have brought to light the fact that the child, Nikki , had been chronically ill most of her life, and most especially in the week before her death. They say doctors who have reviewed her records, as well as slides of her lung tissue, have concluded that Nikki likely died from undiagnosed pneumonia, made worse by drugs prescribed to her by doctors in the days before her death. Other blunt force injuries to the child's head noted by the medical examiner could be explained by the sick child's fall off a bed as well as efforts made by her doctors in the hospital to save her life, her attorneys contend. Terre Compton , one of the jurors who convicted Roberson, told the House committee Monday that had she known all of that, she would not have voted to convict Roberson. She also repeatedly testified that prosecutors at the time made it clear that this was solely a "shaken baby" case. So insistent were they, she recalled, that in driving home their case they violently shook, in front of jurors, either a stuffed bear or doll to demonstrate how Roberson killed his daughter. Compton's testimony is significant because the district attorney today, as well as the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals, has said that Roberson is not eligible for a new trial because his conviction was not solely based on the "shaken baby" diagnosis but also evidence that Nikki sustained other injuries. But evidence of other signs of abuse has now been seriously called into question and may be explained by other things. Compton told the committee she now thinks Roberson is innocent. Of course, Compton is one of only many involved in the case who now have serious doubts. They include the former lead detective, who says the state got it all wrong; more than 80 bipartisan lawmakers who have petitioned the criminal appeals court to reconsider the case; Phil McGraw and author John Grisham, both of whom told the committee that they fully investigated the case and believe Roberson did not get a fair trial; even U.S. Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor, who took the unusual step last week of publicly saying that Roberson has made a "serious showing of actual innocence." Can all those people be wrong? Or did the state get it wrong? Did the criminal appeals court, which ruled just 5-4 earlier this month to uphold the execution, consider the full facts? We note that the appeals court, on its own power and authority, could reconsider and grant Roberson a new trial based on the state's junk science law. Just one vote would need to change. We urge it to do so. We also note that Anderson County District Attorney Allyson Mitchell, who was not in office at the time of Roberson's conviction, could also reconsider the case in light of Compton's testimony and other details revealed at the House committee hearing. We urge her to do so, as well. And finally we urge our governor, a lawyer himself, to look carefully at the facts in this case and to ask himself, given all we know now, given all of the doubt that has been raised, whether our state can in good conscience put this man to death. This editorial board is not a trier of fact, but in light of so much overwhelming evidence and the extraordinary acts of a group of bipartisan legislators in recent days, Roberson deserves a new day in court." He has pressed Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson to request that the federal government hand over data the state could use to cross-check its voter rolls. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services on Oct. 10 to a that states may use to verify individuals' naturalized or acquired citizenship status. Immigration officials have gone back and forth with officials in several states over the data it can provide. "The Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program is the most secure and efficient way to reliably verify an individual's citizenship or immigration status, including for verification regarding voter registration and/or voter list maintenance," the agency's director, Ur M. Jaddou , wrote to Nelson, adding that the agency "currently cannot offer an alternative process to any state." The , meanwhile, argued that the program is "not an adequate tool, on its own, for a state seeking to verify the citizenship status of an individual on the voter rolls." LOCAL GOVERNMENT "Hollins calls for ethics probe into Whitmire's State of the City ," Houston Chronicle's Abby Church -- "Controller Chris Hollins penned a letter Tuesday to the Office of the Inspector General and City Council Ethics Committee calling on Mayor John Whitmire 's to be included in requested against him. Whitmire asked for the investigation into Hollins after he solicited sponsorships for Tuesday's City of Houston Investor Conference -- Hollins' first as controller. In a Thursday news conference, Whitmire said banks called and told him the sponsorships gave the appearance of a "pay to play" system. Hollins fired back later in the day and called Whitmire a "walking conflict of interest," saying the State of the City address featured plenty of sponsors with city contracts. Whitmire wrote in a statement Tuesday that the investigation requested is "in response to (Hollins) soliciting $100,000 from vendors for a private meeting with him." The mayor added that he did not solicit sponsorships for State of the City and that the "controller's attempt to divert attention from the appearance of the pay to play is under investigation." "It is the practice of the mayor's office not to comment on active investigations," Whitmire wrote. "I did my job by bringing this to light." The letter obtained by the Chronicle states that the controller's office used the same fundraising model the mayor used for the State of the City event. According to the letter, those similarities included: Both events being marketed to city vendors Both events selling sponsorships Both featuring VIP receptions for those who gave large monetary contributions Both using their respective official's names and likenesses in marketing the events Both providing respective visibility of both offices The only difference in the events, Hollins wrote in his letter, was who controlled the proceeds. The mayor controls the money for the State of the City, he said, while funds from the Investor Conference went to BankOn Houston and an independent body. "Bias has no place in public service," Hollins wrote in a Tuesday statement. "What's good for the goose is good for the gander. Let me be clear: I do not consider the marketing practices of either event to be unlawful. But I do believe the same set of rules should apply equally to both the mayor's and controller's fundraising activities." He continued: "By applying equal scrutiny to both our offices, we can ensure fairness, transparency and adherence to ethical standards across all levels of City government. This approach will not only address current concerns, but also set a precedent for accountability in future fundraising activities by City officials." The conference, in its ninth year, asked for sponsorships for the first time, Whitmire said. Those sponsorships ranged from $10,000 to $100,000 and each offered varying benefits." ($) "Advocacy group seeks court order to delay Thursday council vote on Austin police contract ," Austin American-Statesman's Ella McCarthy -- "The Austin City Council's much-anticipated vote on a new police union contract could be delayed following an eleventh-hour legal maneuver. The advocacy group Equity Action on Tuesday filed an amended petition in state district court that could force the city to remove the proposed five-year contract from Thursday's city council meeting agenda. As of publication, a judge had not ruled on the petition or held a hearing on the matter. The city of Austin did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Equity Action, which advocates for progressive public safety policies, last December over alleged violations of the Austin Police Oversight Act, a police accountability measure the group crafted and successfully placed on an election ballot earlier that year. Voters overwhelmingly approved it. In that suit, the group argued that the city had failed to "enforce the essential provisions" of the act, which restored the responsibilities of police accountability and transparency to the Office of Police Oversight. The civilian office had previously lost this authority in court arbitration in 2021. in favor of Equity Action on allegations specifically related to the so-called "g-file," a confidential personnel file held by the Police Department for each officer that includes unsubstantiated complaints lodged against them. Other aspects of the lawsuit are still being litigated. Equity Action filed Tuesday's petition in the same case. In the petition, the group alleges that certain language in the agreed upon by the Austin Police Association and the city "is inconsistent with [Austin Police Oversight Act] in multiple respects." Equity Acton says a few tweaks to the contract language would address the group's concerns. "The changes we have requested are simple and would make the words on the page of the agreement match the words in the mouths of the city staff and, more recently, APA leadership," Chris Harris , board president of Equity Action, said in a news release. Throughout the bargaining process, which started in March and ended in September, city negotiators said the city attorney, now Deborah Thomas in an interim capacity, would not support a contract that did not feel complied with the act. Thomas, who is the final arbiter of major city policies, recently issue a memo that said she believes that it does comply. Michael Bullock , president of the police association, recently told the city council that he agrees with the city's interpretation of the language relating to the g-file. "I am undeterred." Bullock told the Statesman Wednesday. "I am confident that this contract is beneficial for our city, for the police department. It removes the barriers to oversight."" ($) #TXLEGE "Delta-8 hemp and Texas medical marijuana industries to face off in the upcoming legislative session ," Texas Tribune's'Stephen Simpson -- "Jack Stinnett got life-changing news in 2020 when he learned the lump that appeared on the side of his neck was tongue and mouth cancer. He and his wife Karen quickly enrolled him at MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, where he underwent five and a half rounds of chemotherapy and 33 treatments of radiation. During this time, Stinnett, a Marble Falls resident, went from a reasonably healthy 60-year-old who rode his bicycle more than 60 miles daily to losing more than 100 pounds after losing his appetite and sense of taste. Then, Stinnett qualified for a medical marijuana prescription for the nerve pain he received from the cancer treatments and found the relief he needed. "It helped with my appetite and sleep. This Compassionate Care Act, in my opinion, helps like no other," he said. "We just need politicians to get out of the way." Stories like this point to the successes of Texas' Compassionate Use Program, but it is facing its worst existential crisis since its inception in 2015. Strict rules on who is eligible, what products can be sold, and where they can be stored have limited the program's impact, while unregulated hemp products like delta-8 and the more potent delta-9 continue to rise in demand due to ease of access. A potential showdown is brewing between the medical cannabis market and the hemp industry in Texas as both are looking to lawmakers to determine the future. States like Colorado and California, where both medical and recreational marijuana are legal, are putting tighter restrictions on hemp products as a way to rein in access and force more health and safety accountability on the industry. After his 2019 agricultural hemp legislation helped open up Texas's hemp industry, state Sen. Charles Perry is now attempting to close it again, as legal weed-style products were never his intention. He suggested an outright ban on the consumable hemp market last week during a State Affairs Committee hearing. "'If you can't regulate it, control it, and enforce it, you just don't allow it to happen," Perry said. Perry and other lawmakers have been particularly interested in regulating consumable THC products that can come in drink form. This makes it much more difficult for parents, teachers, law enforcement, and others to tell the difference between a regular drink and one that has been infused with THC. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick gave senators a for the next session, and a prime target is a ban on delta-8 products. He suggested to lawmakers that the state examine the sales of intoxicating hemp products in Texas, make recommendations to regulate the sale of these products, and propose legislation to stop retailers who market these products to children. The Texas Department of State Health Services also before the state's Supreme Court in August to classify as an illegal substance. While the case is pending, delta-8 is still legal to buy and sell. The Texas hemp industry has argued in court that delta-8's high is minimal, and if delta-8 and delta-9 products are banned, it would do irreparable harm to the industry and the state's economy. "Any bans or excessive legislation of hemp-derived cannabinoids, as suggested by Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick and others, will negatively impact an industry that has an $8 billion economic impact, pays $1.6 billion in annual wages, and supports more than 50,000 workers," said Lukas Gilkey , CEO and co-founder of Hometown Hero, the company who filed a suit against the state and is defending the hemp industry in the state's Supreme Court." | **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

Chuck Schumer and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee are now jumping into this race to rescue endangered career politician Martin Heinrich. They’re funneling out-of-state dollars into New Mexico to buy up precious advertising time during the final weeks and days before Election Day. They know they were completely caught off guard when I entered this race and have been watching nervously as we’ve gradually caught up to Heinrich in the polls. Now, they can’t stand to sit by any longer and are frantically trying to stop our upward momentum. With New Mexico being one of the smallest states and cheapest media markets in the 2024 fight for the Senate, the money they’ve raised from West and East Coast liberal elites stretches much further here, which means they can do A LOT more damage with much less. But that also means your support goes much further here, We’ve never been so close to flipping a “safe blue” state, and I need every bit of support you can send down the home stretch. Let’s keep up the fight! Nella Domenici Republican for Senate | ABOUT NELLA New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years. Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant. Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans. Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. We made a very difficult decision last week.
We had a campaign team meeting, during which it became clear that if we had a bit more money, we could make a real play for additional votes as voting was underway across the state.
The money wasn’t in the budget. But I gave the green light.
It’s a risk. But this is the moment to take some risks. I’ve had similar moments in prior years. We can’t get caught short when people are already casting their ballots in this election. That'd be a mistake.
But the bet we made was that, as the race tightens, and if we asked, our supporters would come through to help fill the gap. We hope that you will. To keep the Senate in the hands of the Democrats.
So with that in mind: can you make a $10 contribution to Tim Kaine and my campaign to help us fill the budget gap we created going after the voters we need to persuade to help win this race? $10 isn’t much, but at this point it’s the small-dollar donations that are making a difference here at the end.
Like I said, it was a tough call. But if there’s one thing that distinguishes this campaign from every other, it’s our people. You answer the call every single time. $10 is all we need to close the gap. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-slotkin]

name: Dave McCormick
subject: Before you sit down for dinner, I hope you'll take just 1 minute to read this personal story
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Dave McCormick
body:
This powerful story follows the journeys of two Army officers
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNETGcLl5HwjQUk4V8EHhSiIhQ0lEd7oAl6HAqTbMZIk2IUM9oPSEbnvxYKpRUZ-UPxwvDnDPALzRG2Os9ApLKpp39LuMwRnOyx7f9aSHVQAZj4v0dcfeE7Vb2f0zflajllT_UoXCvqOGiRGGwaWi3oWQ%3D%3D)

Peter,

Before you sit down for dinner, will you take a minute to read this?

As I am on the campaign trail, I'm reminded of the great sacrifices that are made every day to defend our country. Today, I hope you'll take just a few minutes to hear this personal story directly from me.

Nearly four decades ago, during my time at West Point, I came across a book that left a lasting impact on me. **[It was"Once an Eagle" by Anton Myrer.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNEK2tATcP6VvzbM8_VZrqH6gjpQioOmfasWr4AhvziiwxbpCC-fXiG48WcDeGQ2piJWPEBApHim5RUWcnIFh1idZi_qySMz2-jZg7sg_h4xVd6QjA4LGYbIp2IIAnSP4zha8_m43VNR7L5YIDKrPs-7Q%3D%3D)**

This powerful story follows the journeys of two Army officers - one who navigated his career driven solely by personal gain and advancement, and one who navigated his career by putting the well-being of his fellow soldiers above all else.
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNEvoMg8c5HdTrG_-HlrXvfAwEDk936Zzuj3ZAXmDb4C6SRIpG5YeWavRB88yUvz1xvMfWRNae-myGyzGU8X8-HsTLpgkYZW7VE9fLEM3vsWoBDBodmWMYBkuQp01nrOR_TrCFNA1Ms3sXPq2YlW-lduA%3D%3D)
After graduating from West Point, I went into the Army. It was then that I truly reflected on this book and one very important lesson it taught me.

**[True leadership is not about you. It is about selfless service to others and to the mission.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNESLxexkDHwcOWlPArJHsbOpnQ6viiFZe1DhygpglIJNMTornppmvFF9ARbMn6OJcpBqd8u66FWufKcLDuuwpqKiNErF31FrNcYjnxlb3DIXgNCyGLuKsiC3fPsJuvj9OePdTQsj9_6a-sdzjSCXhz-A%3D%3D)**
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNEIA1oC5b1TNLNCM42bqyD9ckkyXUEfLIavqBj4ZKmKu_p8yQYPBtEHm51kkc1U-42gIMzhWsJJDuz4NfaL3b75pXAcNvBJrSJ1oj8TY3v-hDin__8KWVwzTnXG-kxokUVNrXmBK7QajqbswjNzOqjaw%3D%3D)
As a combat vet, the days are long and hard. You're deep in the heart of a grueling trek, the weight of your pack bearing down with each step.
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNE2d38xUBHYjH5ovoSpQTYhYaWPyZXYoZ_PejOQYM9dmjZ1atZC2wnayGaEMDzRLa7wjvfh8BZ_ExW5WJTJG4SgiJfRfuYusAVimYERvLlPTxlSmarKqVZRI3mHsgQna1C5yc2pTAWiG4GkxTYVfJsuA%3D%3D)
In the heat of the moment, even the smallest blister can feel like a mountain to overcome.
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNENxSJIAiazTY_ZRVVwDwVtFRLJ4NaetTJRHaFkiZEo5OKEysAU8cL7Q4EGJZevd4-lB9dMBeAUV4BeooXIvSZWQ7Jtk3JCrVoi4WpazF9hhpvtHMmI8xzTyrp31hPDp29lV4B-ldyC5qYxRn2tdnErA%3D%3D)
**[As a platoon leader in the 82nd Airborne, I've been there.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNE6EeKYK-cE1V9CVbpOVVhAQB0HN_O5r4_4xiAKXLcRQWY_AwVqEMyZW69VqCEBTC1BvI1NI-8NvonA4FRRA_HVntPh_ECgSujma3y1dk3GRWeSfMiRCpFFmOUQqlR-cOOtiGbdlPMpW8ijwQlHHuRfg%3D%3D)** After hours of marching, it's not easy to keep pushing through pain. But, no matter what, I remembered how important it was to check my soldiers' feet before my own.

**[Why? Because great leaders ALWAYS put others' needs first.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=2e3e0e32607f4e75953a757edc0e99ba&_e=goFbcdD8zIxq5XApc7P0G4W17EbW4bNaSZ7wXPLDIld_47Kkmd4Oxxm0iN1y40j3b151dZXGGuR7f1Ymz47ObW_sp3zEVHbDNPls0I1cWnxkkeYZxTk-HHkbbcBFCwZ7Tn5b7_aUi9IJVz49nn3AmSQ3ytFHCQIOCmGuglgdJipSbG50fA945E63HXngRLnG3CUicWd6X2Wz3F2Oqv7NQMSInQIaienReJXr9TcOD7z2qlRkGrj3JGttgLNqphNEg8UkVTh4WjNW37aeJ5RwabP3oOxilqkL6T68jYZA4WUKpN9gQs342aoGUk0VuH-0cQa-iCu3Z8HFNx2JWMxvORSLka2jH0i_nHX7fVDDugWCcYkGNWWeNSlQkR40b-2ppJrugXqObI08R7fIq5tt2w%3D%3D)**

WHO HAS THE COURAGE TO STAND UP FOR YOU?

---
| [](https://byh4wqwab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001eDJ6N9opLU5o74rLdXNehyxJ1KMUQmFfvmmZw2Anl38PlB-Q-O-L6tuccqgvxFqCIFVK8igCq5S_jXglVL4abp2a6Xp7MNq4hyKEnyzxv0Nc-IR4Wyvng01hCQ3sSAlyJsXDUrrBqwH1ixCJ05SZitkH2I_o7PxNlrSguA6AjhrFqoU4lRCImQ==&c=tjYddU-voCmrzBI8O7eN2cuyzwlVts0zBLemPbz7Xda9qayfpQ5NXg==&ch=HQbstAcBw8yJXFJRO-GFjPcnlLYtAKrZeyNBBQqErtqb6h8c9G0b5g==)
---
| Friends, This is still painful to watch. But you need to watch it.
If they will do this to me, they will do this to you. Who will stand in the gap for you?
I will. I already have.
When the going gets tough, will your representative cave into the pressure to "go along, to get along," with the political establishment in Richmond?
Or will your representative take a stand for you? Will they challenge the status quo, as I did during the assault on our liberties "during Covid," and after the 2020 Presidential Election was stolen?
Standing comes at a cost. They wanted to shut me up. But I would not stop speaking truth to power.
Politicians did not want me to talk about the 2020 Presidential Election being stolen.
But I did. It was the right thing to do.
Our Constitutional rights were being decimated during Covid, and I refused to be silent.
So the Democrat controlled Virginia Senate with the help of 3 Republicans voted to censure me illegally on Tuesday, January 26, 2021.
A censure is a mostly symbolic gesture of disapproval and doesn't affect a legislator's ability to serve. However, that didn't stop the Democrat controlled Virginia Senate from stripping me of my committee assignments and my seniority. It was the price I had to pay for standing.
The Democrat controlled state senate illegally censured me in an attempt to shame me into submission. There are only 2 Virginia Senators in the history of Virginia to be censured, and I unexpectedly made history.
Democrat Lieutenant Governor Justin Fairfax said the censure was "not properly before the Senate." The censure was illegal. The Senate of Virginia failed to follow their own rules, the very rules they were accusing me of breaking.
They failed to conduct an investigation, and in fact used the words the press's interpretation of what I said to convict me.
It was a politically motivated sham censure meant to break me.
But it didn't work.
After they stripped me of my last committee assignment, I prayerfully decided to run for governor.
I was the front runner for Governor. And then they de-platformed me on Facebook and the State Central Committee opted for an unassembled Ranked Choice Voting convention, that confused most voters on when and where to vote.
So many voters expressed their frustration to me. They wanted to vote but the process was confusing. There was paperwork to be completed and deadlines, that in some cases were only one week.
Republican voters who wanted to participate in the nomination process for choosing our next Republican nominee for Governor found the voting process confusing. Many missed the arbitrary deadlines that were different for each county and many voters who wanted to participate could not. They had missed the arbitrary deadlines.
There were Republican voters who were not members of their local GOP who had a difficult time figuring out how to vote. When I returned the Senate, I voted to end confusing party processes that disenfranchise and discourage Republicans from voting and choosing our Republican nominees.
While some Republicans support this confusing party processes to chose our Republican nominees, I consistently support processes that voters are most familiar with and allow legal recourse for bad actors. This legislation went into effect July 2024 but does not apply to Special Elections, like the one we will have this coming December and January.
If you live in Senate District 10, which includes Amelia, Appomattox, Buckingham, Cumberland, Prince Edward, Fluvanna, Goochland, Henrico, Hanover, Louisa or Powhatan, you will most likely vote in November, December and January. Please be on the look out after this November's General Election for a Special Election to be called to fill an open state senate seat to be vacated by John McGuire who who is expected to win this November.
Republicans will chose their nominee in December or January with the General Election expected to be January 7, the day before the General Assembly gavels in. So please stay tuned. There will be an announcement of a Special Election and then 5 days later we are expected to come up with a Republican nominee.
Typically a replacement would be selected by only a handful of party faithful who are aware of the election. I started back in July educating you about this Special Election, so that you could be made aware and demand to be included in selected our Republican nominee. It's important that McGuire's successor is chosen by We the People. This is no time for inexperience, which is why I threw my hat in the ring to run back in July, as the first candidate to announce.
In July, I fully committed to running for this state senate seat and bought a home in conservative Appomattox, where I plan to reside indefinitely.
Those who have followed me know I have both the experience and conservative voting record to hit the ground running on day one, when session will already be in progress.
While there are many Republicans vying for the seat, I'm the only candidate who will be ready day one when session is already in progress.
Talk is cheap. Actions count.
While many will say they support issues important to conservatives, yet I'm the only one running with an actual conservative voting record to prove it.
While there are a number of candidates seeking the Republican nomination for State Senate in Senate District 10 to finish John McGuire's state senate term, I'm the only candidate who has a proven voting record you can trust 100% of the time.
I have a conservative voting record you can trust all 8 years I served in the Virginia Senate:
100% Pro-family, The Family Foundations scorecard, 2016-2023
100% Pro-gun, VCDL Virginia Citizen's Defense League, 2016-2023
A rating, NRA, 2016-2023
100% Pro-small business, National Federation of Independent Business, 2016-2023.
You can trust me. I'm experienced. I have a conservative voting record you can trust, and I'm willing to stand when it's important to stand on our conservative principles. Sometimes that means speaking up and challenging the status quo.
You have the opportunity to support an award winning effective conservative senator with 8 years of experience as a senator and a 100 percent conservative voting record you can trust and who knows how to win for the people.
Today, I ask for your vote if you live in Amelia, Appomattox, Buckingham, Cumberland, Fluvanna, Goochland, Louisa, Prince Edward, Henrico, Hanover and Powhatan in the upcoming Special Election.
If you live outside the district, I ask for your most generous donation. You may not be able to vote for me, but I can certainly vote for you.

# THE ORIGINAL CENSURE
---
| February 2021, I was running for Governor. The campaign finance report numbers had just been released and I was the front runner for Virginia Governor.
Two candidates, both millionaires, had just announced they were running for governor and within 48 hours of their announcements, I was being censured on the floor of the Virginia Senate. The timing was not lost on me, nor my supporters.
Democrat Senator John Bell was the original sponsor of SR91 Senate Resolution 91. 9 other Democrat Senators joined in as co-patrons of the Senate Resolution.
Here's what I was accused of in the original censure:
* Falsely stating that I had violated the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution by engaging in insurrection to overturn the 2020 election results
* For calling J6ers patriots who love their country

Dr. Robert Malone was the inventor of the Covid vaccine. Although he took the jab, he later withdrew his support and is now actively exposing the truth about the side effects of the vaccine, to include death. Dr. Paul Marik spoke as a subject matter expert on several of my medical freedom bills. People want choice not mandates. | STANDING FOR THE 2ND AMENDMENT | Many of you heard me speak at the 2020 VCDL Legislative Day at the Capitol when there were well over 50,000 gun loving Virginians who arrived in Virginia. You can trust me to protect your gun rights. To me it's personal. You can trust me to stand up for the 2nd Amendment. | | | == | | == Senator Amanda Chase has a 100% rating from VCDL all 8 years she served in the Virginia Senate from 2016-2023. | | | | | | | | | | | Some politicians say that they support the 2nd Amendment. I have both a public history and legislative record of opposing gun control. Action should trump rhetoric. I've actually introduced legislation to repeal the gun control laws that the Democrat controlled General Assembly passed in 2020. | | After I was assaulted on multiple occasions on Capitol grounds, I decided to open carry. It worked. The national protestors that flooded our state capitol finally stopped laying hands on me. I believe with all of my heart that guns save lives. I also believe an armed society is a polite society. | | | Many have taken this picture out of context. My team and I were standing on Bank Street in front of the Virginia Capitol in Richmond with hundreds of pro-2nd Amendment supporters from all walks of life. | | July 4, 2020, I was asked to be speak at a Pro-2nd Amendment Rally in downtown Richmond at our state capitol. I was told it was too dangerous to go. Both Antifa and BLM were supposed to be there. My security team and I made the decision to go anyway. Keep in mind the Richmond Police and just been demoralized by Democrat Mayor Levar Stoney. This picture was taken in the streets of Richmond. | The Democrat Trifecta of 2020 passed scores of gun control legislation like one gun a month, universal background checks, red flag laws and gun free zones could not be created by localities. I spoke out against these bills that were a violation of both our U.S. Constitution and our Virginia Constitution. The Democrats controlled the Virginia Senate, the Virginia House and Governor Ralph Northam was Governor. Legislatively, there was nothing we could do. We didn't have the votes. So I chose to go public and expose to the American people what the Democrats were doing. | Bloomberg and others nefarious actors were dumping millions of dollars into Virginia. It was an all out war on our 2nd Amendment rights. While I knew we didn't have the votes, I chose to be creative and get vocal. | To implement socialism, I knew they would first come for our guns. And they did. Instead of protecting individual rights for people to protect themselves, the Democrats were more interested in protecting the criminals, including violent offenders. | SENATOR CHASE TARGET PRACTICE | == | | STANDING UP FOR INNOCENT LIFE THOSE WHO CAN'T SPEAK UP FOR THEMSELVES | The Pro-family, non-profit group, The Family Foundation issues a legislative scorecard so that Virginians can see how their legislator scores on pro-family issues. For my entire 8 year legislative career, year after year from 2016 through 2023, I received a perfect score of 100%. You can trust that I will stand for life, because I have a voting record you can trust. Not just my words. | | Life begins at fertilization. Even 98% of scientists agree. I introduced a Life Begins at Conception bill. The Senate Rules Committee refused to make a motion to vote up or down on the bill. If they voted for the bill, they would have to agree that life begins at conception. If they voted down the bill, they would oppose the opinion of 98% of scientists. | == Watch as I present SR87 Life Begins at Conception bill on | | I've been honored to speak at Family Foundation organized pro-life rallies at the Virginia State Capitol. After SCOTUS overturned the Landmark Roe vs Wade Case, CNN asked for an interview. I'm not afraid to stand for life. | | | == | I led the effort in the Virginia Senate to defeat the so called Equal Right Amendment, a failed amendment that was resurrected from the 70s. The false claim was that it should be passed to give women equal rights and codify it in the Constitution. The real agenda was to promote gender fluidity, a concept that seemed so foreign until today. I was an outspoken leader against the so called Equal Rights Amendment. Listen as I speak against SJR 284 on the floor of the Virginia Senate. | == | I've worked under two Democrat governors and one Republican governor. There are different strategies that have to be used for each. Under a Democrat governor, we know pro-life legislation will not pass. So do we continue to introduce legislation even when we know it will not pass? I believe that we should and I do. It's important that we put legislators on the record so that voters know how they will vote when we do have the votes and it does count. | | | | | The late Virginia Senator Eva Mae Scott (R-Amelia) and I speak at a press conference organized by The Family Foundation against the so-called Equal Rights Amendment. | STANDING UP FOR SECURE ELECTIONS MAKING SURE YOUR VOTE COUNTS | | When voters in my senate district went to cast their vote in 2020, many said that they couldn't vote because someone had already cast their vote for them. I was determined to investigate and get to the bottom of this, despite efforts to be shamed into not questioning the 2020 Presidential Election results. | | I flew to Arizona to witness the first ever full forensic audit so that I knew what legislation to introduce in Virginia. Clearly there was a national effort to steal our elections and what they were doing in Arizona was happening all across the country, but only Republican controlled legislators were able to investigate. I worked very closely with the Arizona legislature. My hope was to have a full forensic audit right here in Virginia, but the legislature was completely controlled by the Democrats. So I sought to expose what was happening across the country, and eventually right here in Virginia. | | Pictured: Arizona State Senator Wendy Rodgers, Senator Amanda Chase, Representative Mark Finchem and Senator Sonny Borrelli. | | The Voter Confidence Restoration Act was just one of many bills that I introduced to put the guardrails back on our Virginia elections and restore voter confidence in our elections. While my goal was ultimately a full forensic audit of the 2020 election, I knew that wouldn't happen with a Democrat controlled legislature. So, I led the effort to simply go back to our Virginia Election Law best practices prior to covid, back when we required photo ID to vote, we had an election day instead of an election season and there were no drop boxes. | | While in South Dakota at the Mike Lindell Cyber Symposium I founded the National Election Integrity Caucus for legislators across the country. Together we worked on and shared legislative ideas and bills to assist with our election integrity efforts. | | STANDING UP ON JAN 6 | I was there on January 6. But I did not go into the nation's Capitol. Many of us believed the 2020 Presidential Election was stolen and joining the protest at the Capitol in DC with President Trump to exercise our First Amendment right to free speech and to contest the election results. We were counting on Vice President Mike Pence to do the right thing. Unfortunately, he did not and his political career is over. I stand up for true election integrity. As a result, I was censured by the Virginia Senate with 3 Republicans joining. | | | | STANDING UP FOR SAFER COMMUNITIES LOCKING UP VIOLENT CRIMINALS | Over the past 8 years, I have introduced legislation to support our law enforcement to include the Law Enforcement Bill of Rights. I voted against repealing qualified immunity. | | YOU CAN TRUST ME TO STAND | When you are considering who you are going to support for State Senate in District 10, (Appomattox, Amelia, Buckingham, Cumberland, Prince Edward, Fluvanna, Goochland, Louisa, Powhatan, Hanover and the Shady Grove precinct in Henrico) ask yourself who has the experience to start on Day One? The Republican Mass Meeting to fill Senator John McGuire's seat will likely occur this December 2024. The General Election will likely occur on January 7, 2025, the day before session begins. I am the only candidate running for state senate who will be able to hit the ground running on Day 1. In addition, you know that I'm pro-life, pro-gun, pro-school choice, pro-medical freedom, pro-election integrity because I have a history of fighting for you and have a voting record you can trust. I have 8 years of experience as a Virginia Senate. Plus I have an 8 year voting record you can trust. Today, I humbly ask for your financial support and your vote. | | Virginia State Senator (R-District 11) 2016-2023 | | == | | | | | | | | | == | | == | Authorized and Paid for by Friends of Amanda Chase | | | | Friends of Amanda Chase | P.O. Box 5811 | Midlothian, VA 23112 US | | | | | |

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

| Currently there is a disconnect between U.S. Congress, Senate, and the Executive Branch. They are disjointed and leaving our children behind when it comes to schools. As current Commissioner of Public Education I am ready to take my knowledge to U.S. Congress and make sure students are prioritized.

# Sharon Clahchischilliage Invites President Donald Trump to New Mexico
---
| “Hey Donald Trump,
Sharon Clahchischilliage here. I am a candidate running for U.S. Congress New Mexico District 3. This is an invitation to you to come visit us here in (NM) District 3.
I want you to meet the people who are experiencing the effects of a buffer zone around Chaco Canyon.
I want you to meet the people of Mora County who have been left homeless because they have not been compensated from a fire that occurred two years ago in Mora County.
I want you to experience the people, the ranchers, the farmers, who are experiencing land grabs in their area. I need for you to. come here and see what the government is doing to District 3.
You know what? District 3 is rich. We have the Permian Basin. We have the San Juan Basin. Which is a big concern to the global energy world. We fund 50% of the state budget.
So, consider this a very important invitation President Trump. I need your help. I need you to help me show the people that we care. I need you to help me show the people that we CAN do something for them.”

body:
Baseball was just a welcome distraction from the gloom and malaise that had settled on our country thanks to one failed Democrat policy after another. | | |
---

---
| |
---
---
| | Fellow Patriot,Today, I'm asking you to help me defeat the radical Adam Schiff for a seat in the United States Senate, and we only have 13 days left. Our victory will start a Republican Comeback Rally that folks will be talking about for generations to come.Because when you think about it, those ‘good-ol’ days of the 1970s weren't as good as we tend to first remember.Baseball was just a welcome distraction from the gloom and malaise that had settled on our country thanks to one failed Democrat policy after another. Democrat policies had brought America to its knees.And now, as Yogi Berra used to say, “it's déjà vu all over again.”There's fear of walking down the street because of rampant crime, homelessness, and drug addiction. The cost of living is exploding and for the first time causing more people to leave California. Kamala Harris, Gavin Newsom, Adam Schiff and the rest of the Democrats don’t care one bit that Americans are having a hard time. This race is personal for me. Not only did I grow up in Nevada, but I've known Jacky for years. Long before she was a senator, Jacky worked with my father as a computer programmer in a male-dominated field. Jacky is a smart, strong, and reasonable person who cares deeply about the hardworking people of Nevada and across our country.
Jacky is fighting to lower prescription drug costs, restore reproductive freedom, strengthen workers’ rights, and pass commonsense gun safety reforms. She's also trying to protect us from people like her MAGA opponent, who wants to be another destructive force in the Senate helping Republicans crush affordable health care, ban abortion, and do nothing about the senseless gun violence Nevadans know all too well.
We can do better for Nevada and our country than the lies, greed, and self-interest that Donald Trump and his spineless sycophants in the GOP have in store, friend. Jacky is fighting in the Senate every day to build up this country, not tear it down. And she needs our help.
**Recent polling shows her LOSING GROUND to her extreme MAGA opponent, Sam Brown – and she's running out of time to pull ahead before Election Day.**

Now, they can’t stand to sit by any longer and are frantically trying to stop our upward momentum.

With New Mexico being one of the smallest states and cheapest media markets in the 2024 fight for the Senate, the money they’ve raised from West and East Coast liberal elites stretches much further here, _which means they can do A LOT more damage with much less._

**Nella Domenici**
Republican for Senate

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. subject: A new day for Ohio and the country
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/100067/images/LOGO.jpg]
Friends,
I was SO excited to visit Mansfield High School yesterday for their Meet the Candidate event! This event was so important to me especially since this area has a median income of only $24k/yr. I spoke right to them, their parents, and the heart of their issues.
We had a great meeting with the students, who were really engaged in this election. We talked about all kinds of issues that are important to their generation, and while some of them may not be old enough to vote this year, it’s exciting to see how much they care and how knowledgeable they are. They truly are the future!
The students asked me two REALLY important questions yesterday that I think cut right to the heart of this race:
1.Do you think a representative is supposed to represent their party or their district?
2.With our country being so polarized, how would you unite us?
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20241023_mansfield_school_image1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20241023_mansfield_school_image1]
These questions are exactly why I am running to defeat Jim Jordan.
First, I told them that a representative should always represent their district.
It’s not about extremist party loyalty, personal agendas, or corporate interests. It’s about what people really need and making sure they feel heard. We’re called REPRESENTATIVES for a reason – we’re supposed to REPRESENT people!
Our district has been neglected for 17 years under Jim Jordan, who has voted against every farm bill, every effort to support veterans, seniors, and job creation. Ohio deserves better.
Can you rush a contribution now to tell our farmers, veterans, and seniors that we stand with them in their fight for a better life? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20241023_mansfield_school_link1]

As a former Navy SEAL and combat veteran, I’ve seen my fair share of battle. # Don’t Have Any Regrets Day After The Election!
---
| Dear Friends,
With less than two weeks until the election, the stakes couldn't be higher. The next 13 days will be crucial in determining the direction our country will take. Will we continue the progress we've made over the last 31⁄2 years, or will we return to the chaos of Trump's first term?
This past weekend, thousands of volunteers joined me in Nevada to talk to voters and ensure everyone understands what’s at stake. As millions of Americans are already casting their votes, it's essential that we all do whatever we can to support Kamala's campaign team. They need the resources to effectively communicate their message and counter the onslaught of negative campaign ads funded by Trump's billionaire cronies.
Please consider donating whatever you can today. Additionally, I encourage you to forward this email to your friends and family and ask them to contribute as well. Every bit helps!Thank you for your support!
Best regards,
Asif

subject: It's Not Just Candidates On The Ballot...

body:
There are exceptional ballot initiatives in multiple states this year.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ballot_initiative_support_1&n=1)
---
Wednesday, October 23, 2024 | Peter -- When we think of November elections, we usually think about the candidates on the ballot. But, there are other things to vote on this year. That's right - there are **9 major ballot measures** this year that could reshape the way we vote, impacting more than just this election cycle. **Ranked-Choice Voting and Open Primaries are up** for voters to decide on in five statewide contests and four city-level races on November 5th. The Forward Party believes that government should be responsive to the needs of the people, and these election reforms all move us in that direction. These reforms take us one step closer to true equal representation across the country. Our friends over at FairVote have a great rundown of them. | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=0xj462lKowoTlM5xyWdYNAkSdT8Br7tf8BXPwvyszu2_ndVfEfdmAIGonGHk62Ld&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ballot_initiative_support_1&n=2 "Explore These Initiatives With
FairVote!") [Explore These Initiatives With FairVote!](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=0xj462lKowoTlM5xyWdYNAkSdT8Br7tf8BXPwvyszu2_ndVfEfdmAIGonGHk62Ld&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ballot_initiative_support_1&n=2)
---
### **This Year's Critical Ballot Initiatives**

#### Statewide Initiatives
* **Colorado** \- Proposition 131 would bring Open Primaries and RCV to the state. If this passes, CO will become the largest state in the nation to use RCV.
* **Idaho** \- Proposition 1 will implement Open Primaries and RCV statewide. 94,000 Idahoans signed petitions to get this on the ballot.
* **Nevada** \- Question 3 will implement top-five open primaries statewide. Nevada requires citizen-initiated constitutional amendments to pass a statewide vote _two consecutive elections_ , and this has already passed in once in 2022, so this is the final year!
* **Oregon** \- Measure 117 will implement Ranked Choice Voting statewide in Oregon. It was sent to the ballot by Oregon's legislature, which is the biggest step ever taken by any state legislature on RCV.

#### Citywide Initiatives
* **Washington, D.C.** \- Initiative 83 would create Open Primaries and RCV for all of DC elections, allowing their independent voters access to primary voting for the first time in their history.
* **Richmond, CA** \- Measure L would implement RCV in Richmond, the 9th California city to improve its voting in this way.
* **Oak Park, IL** \- Oak Park residents will vote on RCV this November, looking to follow their fellow voters in Evanston who adopted RCV a few years ago.
* **Peoria, IL** \- A non-binding RCV measure is in place in Peoria, asking voters if RCV should be adopted for state and federal elections.

#### Anti-RCV Measures
* **Alaska** \- Opponents of Alaska's recent change to a "top four" style election are running a campaign to reverse the state's decision after just one cycle. 85% of Alaskans find RCV simple and 62% say they like the election system.

All of these ballot measures are transformational for our elections. If they all pass (and we defeat the anti-RCV measure in Alaska), we'll more than double the number of Americans that use RCV each year, and we'll substantially increase the number of voters have a say in their elections by increasing the number of states with Open Primaries.
The creation of a better government is within our grasp. Follow the link below to find out how you can help!

October 23, 2024
Once upon a time in Connecticut, we had Election Day. You went to your polling place and presented a pleasant lady with your ID. She looked at a list and confirmed you were registered and then crossed out your name, indicating that you had voted. You then walked into a booth and closed the curtain behind you. There was a large silver apparatus that listed the names of the candidates with levers you turned for your choices. When you were done, you pulled a handle, and this machine tabulated your vote.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e6ef012b-71bf-4df9-a413-371664919de6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Voting Machine Used in Connecticut Until the 1990s
When it was 8:00 PM, the polls closed. These pleasant people recorded the number of votes for each candidate, under the watchful eyes of representatives of both parties. The Secretary of the State's office was called with the results. State employees added up the numbers and posted the results.
No computers. No one suspecting the computer changed their vote. No hanging chads. No dubious signature verification. No drop boxes. Unless the election was close, the good people of Connecticut knew the winner by 11:00 PM and they trusted the result.
How quaint.
Variations of this system are still used in most of the western democracies. Argentina, France and England recently had elections and voters knew who won the same day - with the results trusted by both sides.
But as Clinton advisor and former Chicago Democratic Mayor Rahm Emanuel stated, "Never let a crisis go to waste."
America's ruling class is no longer trusts the pesky voters to rubber stamp their agenda, especially after President Trump won in 2016. Thus, they used the COVID crisis to normalize mail-in ballots and ballot harvesting making unproveable fraud easier and decreasing voters' trust in the system, especially when these ballots were dumped after the walk-in votes were tabulated.
Voters are skeptical when one candidate has a significant lead (almost always the Republican) on Election Day that evaporates once absentee and mail-in ballots are counted. When this happened to President Trump in 2020, it caused a riot on our Capitol.
Thus, Connecticut voters now have [the following question](https://substack.com/redirect/981fb45b-1ebb-41ce-b88b-f9e79d74bf43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the ballot:
_" Shall the Constitution of the State be amended to permit the General Assembly to allow each voter to vote by absentee ballot?"_
Sounds innocent, doesn't it?
It is not.
Presently, our state constitution requires that you can only request an absentee ballot [in the following circumstances:](https://substack.com/redirect/5300df83-84ca-4365-abf8-f528aa827cec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
• An absence from your town on Election Day prevents you from appearing at your polling place,
• You are prevented from appearing at your assigned polling place on Election Day because of sickness or physical disability (not necessarily your sickness or disability),
• Active service in the military
• Religious tenets forbid secular activity on the day of the election
• Duties as an election official at a polling place other than your own during all of the hours of voting.
Amending our constitution will just encourage fraud. How do we know? Because it has already happened.
Democratic party operatives will use bogus addresses to request ballots. This is what happened in a Bridgeport Democratic primary in 2023. A Democratic operative Wanda Geter-Pataky was caught on videotape depositing illegally harvested absentee ballots, filling them out and placing hundreds of ballots into a drop box. Of course, no charges have been leveled against her. According to state authorities, this is part of an "ongoing investigation."
But [Bridgeport's Chief-of-Police](https://substack.com/redirect/096d931a-48cf-4a65-aee4-48be6990a3a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has already weighed in. He was upset the video of the fraud had been leaked!
Voting should be a community event as our Yankee forefathers realized that this encourages harmony and cooperation. We see our neighbor volunteering to give us our ballots and checking off our names. We see our friends - even ones we disagree with - holding a sign or passing out palm cards for their candidate. We often see the candidates themselves smiling and waving and asking for our votes. This encourages goodwill among people who disagree. And in these polarized times, nothing is worse than having this good will dissipated by faceless mail-in contests.
Remember when you vote on this issue, the question may be located in a different spot than the names of the candidates. It may even be on the back side of your ballot. But it is there. There is a considerable drop off in the number of people voting on ballot issues because the voter was unaware of the ballot issue, or did not bother to check the ballot carefully. Find this question on your ballot and vote "No."

Hi there, Over the years, I’ve been lucky enough to meet and work alongside some of the most passionate grassroots supporters in the climate movement. And if you’re reading this, you’re one of them! It’s supporters like _you_ who keep us moving forward, even when the challenges seem overwhelming. So today, I wanted to do something a little more personal to say thank you. As you know, I’ve been traveling all over the country these past few months, rallying support for Kamala Harris and JanePAC’s down-ballot climate champions. After Election Day, I’m going to send out signed postcards — a special memento from the road — to a couple of amazing supporters who take action this week. **[If you chip in to JanePAC using this link, you might just get one from me! It’s a small — but hopefully, meaningful — gesture to show my immense appreciation for your commitment to this movement.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/95671965/507506563/824180983?refcode=ea.60bddf94-8b91-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&ms=ea.60bddf94-8b91-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjYwYmRkZjk0LThiOTEtZWYxMS04NDc0LTAwMGQzYTk4ZmE2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=g4XXuPWaJuYYo016bh6EXbM5zS2cGl7wK0jlPX36HLw=)** | [**DONATE**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/95671966/507506564/824180983?refcode=ea.60bddf94-8b91-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&ms=ea.60bddf94-8b91-ef11-8474-000d3a98fa6b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjYwYmRkZjk0LThiOTEtZWYxMS04NDc0LTAwMGQzYTk4ZmE2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=g4XXuPWaJuYYo016bh6EXbM5zS2cGl7wK0jlPX36HLw=)

If I’ve learned anything from my travels this election year, it’s this: The most powerful force in any movement isn’t the politicians or the lobbyists or the wealthy special interests cutting checks. It’s A LOT of honest people who show up, stay engaged, and keep pushing forward.
When thousands of people like us take action, we can create lasting change.
That’s why your support means everything, especially as we enter the _final 13 days_ of the most critical election for climate action in our lifetimes. When we unite our voices, our efforts, and our donations, we become an unstoppable force for good.
**[If you’re in a position to give, even a little, it’ll go a long way in helping us keep up the fight to elect climate champions at every level of government. Hi Friend, As we enter the final month of this crucial election cycle, I believe it is imperative that we turn to God with earnest hearts and fervent prayers. The challenges our nation is facing may feel daunting, but as Christians, we are called to be beacons of hope and light.

While casting our votes is essential, I also recognize that we have a key opportunity to pray. We need to intercede not only for the candidates but also for the safety and well-being of their families, and most importantly, that God's will prevails.

Are you feeling the weight of this moment? I know I am.

That's why I'm reaching out to share [_Prayer and Politics_](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=043a5dbcbdec4554b9b89bdf1b3e2408&_e=1_AwEMutSjHF6JibRmcy2XJJfcnnYTTl0gdnRhjHvNVT5jqLUKk7uHRMaQfTdVYQoS3LljcgERh9AmfNWRnBloCzAMPAHsHWs1BoUqJ7zmZs-eKNucrwUt612zSuG2p3CgCe-oXnvBRmhuxizIeHpbpyM9g7WFX5tahTYa8lApvndbWVVlNq_5sAX3C_S3WS5MlFaNGoRs79g2Pc5i8dIeu6vqUL17K0zBPOD5QAgw6EvVssouxuSylCxR7VeawvjceS28882_uREVD5n_rKXLL8oCPkdAxoegB2L0LYF4hy8jmy-fiynwtGxZbASSvijD2r3rduuFxuwAul3OEDbSvifOeLjWat0fOccHSm1RaIDDF40GoFS_amMp4K4IIF), a powerful prayer guide designed to equip us for this very season. Prayer is not just an option; it is our duty as believers to pray for our leaders and for the nation we hold dear.

Within the pages of this prayer guide, you'll find:
* How to pray for the protection of candidates and their families.
* Requests for wisdom and discernment in their leadership.
* Calls for God to raise principled leaders who reflect His justice and truth.
* Appeals for God's sovereign will to be done.

As we witness the political landscape, we must not give in to fear or worry. Instead, let Psalm 46:1-2 guide us: "God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore, we will not fear, though the earth give way and the mountains fall into the heart of the sea."

This election is an important time for us to recommit ourselves to prayer. Let us come together as a Christ-centered community, earnestly seeking God's direction and intervention for our nation. Will you join us?

[get _prayer and politics_ >>](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=043a5dbcbdec4554b9b89bdf1b3e2408&_e=1_AwEMutSjHF6JibRmcy2XJJfcnnYTTl0gdnRhjHvNVT5jqLUKk7uHRMaQfTdVYQoS3LljcgERh9AmfNWRnBloCzAMPAHsHWs1BoUqJ7zmZs-eKNucrwUt612zSuG2p3CgCe-oXnvBRmhuxizIeHpbpyM9g7WFX5tahTYa8lApvndbWVVlNq_5sAX3C_S3WS5MlFaNGoRs79g2Pc5i8dIeYFI3IPXM8ZjpzzH_BFed7sT5fClxpD1siiFLP-D6npUoGrj3nB_6_aRxvVehyq5JVB3rUu4Kx-SNvvKYWzyZbsS_AsATpYbmHasCT73Fb5L6IGMlvkR-gRvBU619zmRMuwykgNvFUCTurGI0TJLLq-59prxTzSdeVY0uE9PtgX) Thank you for being a part of this vital prayer needed today. As we move forward in this pivotal month, may we stand firm in prayer for our country and our leaders, trusting that God will have His way.

In prayer with you,

Jamie Janosz
Managing Editor, _Today in the Word_

#
Friend of Life, it's Lila Rose - Founder and President of Live Action. I have an urgent request.

Today, thousands of preborn children will lose their lives in brutal abortions.

As a pro-life person, I know this breaks your heart. You've probably wondered when the killing would end and have even prayed for abortion to go away. But it isn't going away, at least not on its own.

The Supreme Court didn't end abortion, neither political party has shown the willingness and conviction to end abortion, and many states are now doubling down to protect abortion.

We can't keep waiting on the sidelines for someone else to act. We must get involved if we want to stop the killing, save lives, and create a culture that protects life.

Live Action is partnering with pro-life pregnancy resource centers to provide diapers to moms with urgent needs.

[](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=dbaee9706e5d4fd096cf8f6712478303&_e=hu4TIOPXmcOLmlL9M9fud--OHvpouahIbaeF9-k9rXdfrFvS3OdonlgivREwy0bzHNxWl7KhmAoncn6F1hVTCkt_TuguuTKNpzyk6SM05JOSc9rlCzO8YnsWBa7QX5sB6wNvOFO8yPacJr3G2CwjXpb6B5q_o0dX0yCekRISSLsYieJX5NUOo_Gs-AwdAfgwuE_vFQt377ZyU_BY8MMqF8aFNQXHJIJivYNLGsGVR8GD_X8jMbsapOiGoHdRDI1-Yx4Y1ozFycbh-qqFP1T935mm-qBKsb3VBsiF1UZwGNtzJotjfkNmOsxnnR16_tIPcDwcSS6L5ShMlYzAAc86h-qgmUqIGvCbhgvG1-vm7zu2S5enBusO76xrbJ6kHzUiX4UxcOsdGuA5iDofhMXAUQ%3D%3D)
This isn't another opportunity to donate to a cause, this is the opportunity for you to tangibly give to help a single mother, a teenage girl, a hurting couple, just days away from a life-ending abortion choose life.

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=4987f130f2284afb985f9761f9aa59e4&_e=7_iG28dsXb2pbp4W77tSvmd3rZ_kNM_t87dHPF3mn4keyI22tL9dDtbuN69k9rFZhGt872oX97MNev9Xx7mAleDRazHZDou4G7wda-UOskgC05_efpzKQASuuhJlA7doQhxSAJ6_3O0l-gmDxqqRXmGgeVnPbncUf6vAZNw_1OTk03bIcNtGvigqgx0J37qodkX1q2oEETRG1ppdoSX1ftgcDeqkCbMEoYnIOoZfuM5zsEhK6Tp2v2NYOimpeFFhl5dSLNab-1NFK_J2cIqZilFKKpbybxEIv3KiSWse9ju3nQAI4SRB6cSQCoxqd86ZDJPIZ7PaFgX2mmdEqZjxIeLO9sSeIrfHaY9Rhh7Rri1tFK6Bl_fpX3SHoNClkMks-ow3UigURWiB3TJ_CuBEzQ%3D%3D)

**[Why? Because great leaders ALWAYS put others' needs first.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=4987f130f2284afb985f9761f9aa59e4&_e=7_iG28dsXb2pbp4W77tSvmd3rZ_kNM_t87dHPF3mn4keyI22tL9dDtbuN69k9rFZhGt872oX97MNev9Xx7mAleDRazHZDou4G7wda-UOskgC05_efpzKQASuuhJlA7doQhxSAJ6_3O0l-gmDxqqRXmGgeVnPbncUf6vAZNw_1OTk03bIcNtGvigqgx0J37qodkX1q2oEETRG1ppdoSX1ftgcDeqkCbMEoYnIOoZfuM5zsEhK6Tp2v2NYOimpeFFhK0L6PwOsNbaCvvj3ni11_o3Dwk45w0ct8FXfVRuT7SqbyrIg4GkQKsuPjfJ7wiMMqP4X82LUbi90o4nNsxC4R6iXsoPjzb33OwZIk9PxPjOI4269qFZ-5OmljLp9Gc_RFctO2tCi39tzTVKY-5f-fQ%3D%3D)**

clean_body: This powerful story follows the journeys of two Army officers Fellow Patriot, Before you sit down for dinner, will you take a minute to read this? As I am on the campaign trail, I'm reminded of the great sacrifices that are made every day to defend our country. Today, I hope you'll take just a few minutes to hear this personal story directly from me. Nearly four decades ago, during my time at West Point, I came across a book that left a lasting impact on me. This powerful story follows the journeys of two Army officers - one who navigated his career driven solely by personal gain and advancement, and one who navigated his career by putting the well-being of his fellow soldiers above all else. After graduating from West Point, I went into the Army. It was then that I truly reflected on this book and one very important lesson it taught me. As a combat vet, the days are long and hard. You're deep in the heart of a grueling trek, the weight of your pack bearing down with each step. In the heat of the moment, even the smallest blister can feel like a mountain to overcome. After hours of marching, it's not easy to keep pushing through pain. But, no matter what, I remembered how important it was to check my soldiers' feet before my own. I've seen firsthand what great leadership looks like. I've seen that even on our worst days, you have to put the needs of others first. Under the Democrats' leadership, times are tough. We're experiencing skyrocketing inflating, unprecedented crime rates, open borders, and leadership that is destroying the American Dream. I've been on tough missions, but if I'm going to win my next mission to defeat a Democrat who's spent 18 years in DC - and flip the Senate - during this critical fight for Pennsylvania and our great nation's future. Your donation will not only show that my campaign is a force to be reckoned with, but it will also play a vital role in helping fund our campaign in the upcoming days and weeks. I know how to restore strong leadership in our country because I've done it before. We can revitalize the economy, support small businesses, stop Washington's spending sprees, protect our border, and save America's future. But in order to get the job done, it's going to take all hands on deck. Democrats at every level are outraising their GOP opponents. That’s right: Democratic state senator Judy Seeberger (one of our Democracy Defenders that year) won by a few hundred votes, spending $123,922 while her Republican opponent raised $137,143. _That’s why every dollar, every donation — no matter how small — really matters in these tight races._ [Make your donation today to help the NDRC hold the line in battleground states across the country.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/95672496/507508992/1485360112?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_Minnesota_email_20241023-NDRC-Tier1-Minnesota_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20241023-NDRC-Tier1-Minnesota_&utm_campaign=Minnesota&amount=30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjE3NDAxYmRhLThkOTEtZWYxMS04NDc0LTAwMGQzYTk4ZmE2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=7YF8JTU5iNc2H5MPDOyNEejsvntt310Vc4mgw3I7heI=) **Defending a Democratic Majority** That one-vote majority has been able to make great gains on paid and medical leave, workplace protections, voting rights, gun safety and more. clean_body: Here’s why a Democratic trifecta in Minnesota is so essential. | To: NDRC “Team Minnesota” Re: Key dates and razor-thin majorities Peter, there’s a lot at stake in Minnesota this election season. Minnesota’s state legislature hangs in the balance in 2024 — and with it, so does the power to pass new redistricting reforms, continue the state’s amazing progress, and provide a key check on Republican attempts to gerrymander. Control of the Minnesota State House could come down to a handful of votes — and the NDRC is working around the clock to reach as many voters as possible between now and November 5th. = 🗳️ Early voting started: Sept 20th 📩 Last day of in-person early voting: Monday, Nov 4th 🇺🇸 Election Day: Tuesday, Nov 5th Control of the State House Will Be a Nail-Biter In 2022, just 321 votes flipped control of the State Senate to a one-seat Democratic majority and created a blue trifecta with the State House and governorship. That’s right: Democratic state senator Judy Seeberger (one of our Democracy Defenders that year) won by a few hundred votes, spending $123,922 while her Republican opponent raised $137,143. That’s why every dollar, every donation — no matter how small — really matters in these tight races. = Defending a Democratic Majority That one-vote majority has been able to make great gains on paid and medical leave, workplace protections, voting rights, gun safety and more. And it hangs in the balance this November. We simply can’t let up this momentum and must ensure pro-democracy leaders stay in office. From passing free school breakfast and lunch to restoring the voting rights of ex-felons, we cannot watch the progress the Minnesota one-vote majority has accomplished be undone by extremist politicians. = A Special Election in a Pivotal Year A Democratic state senator resigned earlier this year, leaving an even 33-33 split. **Nella Domenici**
